directive: **Permissions** — this stage is where YOU GENERATE each stream's least-privilege permission set, AT PLAN TIME, as part of authoring the fleet. It is not a runtime toggle and not a manual button: for every stream you DERIVE its `commands` (the shell toolchain), per-tool `perm`, write-paths, and `profile` from the project stack + that stream's `owns`/role, then write the whole fleet to plan.db with `bsc-plan fleet set` so each worker auto-runs exactly what it needs and never blocks on a permission prompt. Pipe a FleetPlan JSON (non-overlapping streams, plus recommended/director/topology) to `bsc-plan fleet set`. **Per-stream shape:** `{"id":"…","repo":"…","owns":[…],"issues":[…],"dependsOn":[…],"commands":["cargo","wasm-pack"],"profile":"<id>","perm":{…},"flow":{…}}`. **Generate each stream's `commands`** from the stack + its `owns`/role (a Rust worker → `["cargo"]`; a web worker → `["npm","node","vite","tsc"]`; a Python worker → `["python","pytest"]`) — at launch each becomes an explicit `Bash(<cmd> *)` auto-approve rule. **The app auto-grants a baseline to every worker, so do NOT re-list it in `commands`** (mirrors `BASELINE_READONLY`/`BASELINE_BUILD`/`MANDATORY_BASH` in `console/settings.rs`): the standard read-only navigation/inspection/text tools (`ls`/`cat`/`grep`/`rg`/`find`/`sed`/`awk`/`jq`/…) for every agent, the common build/test toolchains (`cargo`/`npm`/`node`/`vite`/`tsc`/`python`/`pytest`/`go`/`make`/`docker`/…) for doer (worker) streams, and ALWAYS `gh`/`git`/`bsc-plan`. So a stream's `commands` lists ONLY the stack-specific extras NOT in that baseline (e.g. `terraform`, `psql`, `protoc`, `wasm-pack`). **Set each stream's `profile`** to a least-privilege AgentProfile id (or note the app can generate one per stream from role + `owns` + `commands`). **CAVEAT — `Bash(<cmd> *)` rules match the WHOLE command string,** so piped/compound commands (`cargo metadata | python -c …`) and special-char invocations still fall through to a prompt: list the REAL toolchain commands per stream, and have kickoffs prefer simple, single-binary invocations where practical (note a pipeline may still prompt). **Set each stream's `flow` (#297)** as a NESTED object — `"flow":{"autonomy":"continuous|checkpoint|confirm","push":"auto-pr|self-merge|push-confirm|commit-only|none","trigger":"per-issue|per-stage|on-green","gate":"soft|hard"}` — this canonical shape round-trips through `bsc-plan fleet get`; omit a field to take its default (`continuous`+`auto-pr`+`per-issue`+`hard`). (Flat top-level `autonomy`/`push`/`trigger`/`gate` attrs are also accepted on ingest for back-compat, but emit the nested `flow`.) A stream may also carry `mcp` (assigned MCP servers) and `groupIds` (skill task-group ids from `bsc-skill group`, authored in the Skills stage) — each worker inherits those at launch. The fleet lives ONLY in plan.db — there is no fleet.json; `bsc-plan fleet get` shows the stored fleet.
name: Permissions
gate: every stream scoped + shared deps locked

require.label: set a profile for every stream
lock shared deps for any repo 2+ streams build

prompt:
For every work stream, derive a least-privilege profile: allowed commands, write-path globs,
network access, and a git/gh push policy. Map each to a role (worker / director / triage).

**Grant each stream its toolchain** — set the stream's `commands` to the shell commands that
stream legitimately auto-runs, derived from the stack (a Rust worker `["cargo"]`; a web worker
`["npm","node","vite"]`; a Python worker `["python","pytest"]`). These become auto-approve rules so
the agent never prompts for its own build/test commands. A safe read-only baseline (`ls`/`cat`/`grep`/…)
is always allowed and the common build toolchains are pre-approved for doer (worker) streams, so
`commands` only needs the project-specific extras; list anything unusual it must run unattended.

Record the whole fleet IN THE PLAN DB — pipe a FleetPlan JSON to `bsc-plan fleet set` (do NOT write
fleet.json):
  `echo '{"recommended":<n>,"reasoning":"…","director":{"enabled":true,"drive":"…"},"topology":"director|peer|hybrid","streams":[{"id":"…","repo":"…","owns":[…],"issues":[…],"dependsOn":[…],"commands":["cargo","wasm-pack"],"profile":"…","perm":{…},"flow":{…}}]}' | bsc-plan fleet set`
(`bsc-plan fleet get` shows the stored fleet.)

Choose the coordination TOPOLOGY (`topology`): "director" (hub-and-spoke — every relationship routes
through the director), "peer" (mesh — agents hand off directly), or "hybrid" (per-edge, using each
edge's `via`). Set the director `drive` when one is enabled. The user can flip this in the Permissions
pane and the Structure relationship graph re-routes live.

Gate: every stream has a scoped profile and a role.

**Shared dependencies** (#1429) — for any repo that 2+ streams build, each stream declares its libraries and you reconcile them ONCE into the repo's lock so the parallel fleet never redefines them (which collides at integration). Record the manifest with `bsc-plan deps set` (JSON on stdin: a `dependencies` array — each `{repo, ecosystem: npm|cargo, name, version, dev?, why, source?, stream}`, tagging the declaring `stream` — plus a `registries` map defining any non-public `source` with its `url`, `scope`, and `auth` secret NAME). A repo with a SINGLE owning stream needs no pre-lock — its deps stay agent-managed. `bsc-plan deps get` shows the manifest.
